blocks.text: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
heading_path: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

blocks.text: This is the third quarter National Government Budget Implementation Review Report for FY 2018/19 and covers the period from July 2018 to March 2019. It is prepared in line with Article 228 of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010 and section 9 of the Controller of Budget Act, 2016, which requires the Controller of Budget to submit to each House of Parliament a report on the implementation of the budgets of the national and county governments every four months.
heading_path: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

blocks.text: The report presents the progress made in implementing the FY 2018/19 Budget in the first nine months. It presents information on receipts into the Consolidated Fund and expenditure performance, which is analysed by sector, and is further disaggregated by government Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs). Both revenue and expenditure performance is also compared with a similar period of FY 2017/18. The key challenges that affected budget implementation during the period are identified and appropriate recommendations made.
heading_path: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

blocks.text: In the first nine months of the FY 2018/19, total receipts into the Consolidated Fund amounted to Kshs.1.67 trillion representing 64.8 per cent of the revised estimates, recording a growth by 10.6 per cent compared to Kshs.1.51 trillion received in a similar period of FY 2017/18. Total exchequer issues to MDAs and County Governments amounted to Kshs.1.65 trillion , representing 64.4 per cent of the revised net estimates, a growth by 20.4 per cent compared to Kshs.1.37 trillion recorded in a similar period in FY 2017/18. The exchequer issues comprised of Kshs.661.9 billion for MDAs' recurrent expenditure, Kshs.588.9 billion towards Consolidated Fund Services (CFS), Kshs.197.2 billion for development expenditure and Kshs.205.6 billion to the county governments.
heading_path: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

blocks.text: Gross expenditure for MDAs and CFS amounted to Kshs.1.7 trillion representing 63.5 per cent of the revised grossed estimates, an increase compared to 60.2 per cent (Kshs.1.3 trillion), recorded in the first nine months of FY 2017/18. This expenditure comprised of Kshs.1.3 trillion on recurrent activities and Kshs.395.3 billion on development programs. The recurrent expenditure comprised of Kshs.720.6 billion incurred by the MDAs, representing 67.7 per cent of the revised gross recurrent estimates, a 2.6 per cent increase from Kshs.702.5 billion (66.8 per cent), recorded in a similar period of FY 2017/18 and Kshs.584.2 billion on CFS. The CFS expenditure was 60.6 per cent of the revised gross estimates, an increase of 72.2 per cent compared to Kshs.339.3 billion (62.4 per cent), spent in a similar period of FY 2017/18.
heading_path: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

blocks.text: Analysis of the MDA's recurrent expenditure by major economic item indicates that, most expenditure related to; personnel emoluments, current transfers to Semi-Autonomous Government Agencies (SAGAs), travelling, rentals and rates for non-resid ential buildings, and hospitality. Personnel emoluments (PE), recorded the highest expenditure at Kshs.294.7 billion representing 41 per cent of the MDAs' recurrent expenditure. The Teachers Service Commission reported the highest expenditure on PE at Kshs.177.9 billion, which translated to 60 per cent of the PE expenditure by the MDAs. The second highest was on current transfers to SAGAs at Kshs.204.9 billion, representing 28.4 per cent while domestic travel recorded the third highest expenditure at Kshs.7.7 billion representing 1.1 per cent of the MDAs recurrent expenditure.
heading_path: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

blocks.text: The gross development expenditure amounted to Kshs.395.3 billion , recording an absorption rate of 60.8 per cent , an increase by 39.8 per cent compared to Kshs.282.6 billion (46.7 per cent) recorded in a similar period in FY 2017/18. The major expenditure items included; capital transfers to SAGAs, refurbishment of buildings/infrastructure, construction and civil works, and construction of non-residential buildings. The highest expenditure category was capital transfers to SAGAs at
heading_path: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

blocks.text: Kshs.177.4 billion, followed by refurbishment of buildings/infrastructure at Kshs.109.5 billion and construction and civil works at Kshs.30.6 billion, representing 44.9 per cent, 27.7 per cent and 7.7 per cent of the gross development expenditure, respectively.
heading_path: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

blocks.text: In the first nine months of FY 2018/19, implementation of the budget faced some challenges which slowed down execution of planned activities. The challenges included; delay in submission of financial and non-financial reports to the Office of the Controller of Budget by Accounting Officers, which affected timely reporting and consequently, oversight by various Stakeholders; and failure to align budget re-allocation to actual performances in Supplementary Budget I, which lead to reduction of some budget items below the level of expenditure already incurred. The affected MDAs should liaise with the National Treasury to address the anomaly in the Supplementary Budget II.

blocks.text: 1  INTRODUCTION
heading_path: 1  INTRODUCTION

blocks.text: The Office of the Controller of Budget is established under Article 228 of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, to oversee the implementation of the budgets of the national and county governments by authorizing withdrawals from public funds under Articles 204, 206 and 207 and submit a report to each House of Parliament on the implementation of the budgets every four months.
heading_path: 1  INTRODUCTION

blocks.text: This report has been prepared in compliance with Article 228(6) of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, and Section 9 of the Controller of Budget Act, 2016 which require the Controller of Budget to submit to each House of Parliament a report on the implementation of the budgets of the national and county governments every four months. It provides information on budget implementation for the first nine months of FY 2018/19, and compares performance with that of a similar period in the previous financial year.
heading_path: 1  INTRODUCTION

blocks.text: The report is structured into seven chapters. Chapter one offers the introduction. Chapter two provides information on receipts into the Consolidated Fund and exchequer issues to MDAs, Consolidated Fund Services (CFS) and County Governments for funding government programmes.
heading_path: 1  INTRODUCTION

blocks.text: Chapter three presents a summary of overall budget performance in the period under review and is compared to that of a similar period in FY 2017/18. Budget performance is presented both in absolute figures and as a percentage of the budget. Exchequer issues are expressed as a percentage of the revised net estimates while expenditure performance is presented as percentage of the revised gross estimates. Net estimate is the gross estimates less Appropriations in Aid (A-I-A). The chapter also provides expenditure incurred on Consolidated Fund Services, which is categorised as recurrent expenditure and consists of Public Debt; payments for Pensions and Gratuities; Salaries, Allowances and Miscellaneous Services; and, Subscriptions to International Organisations. Further, the chapter provides analysis of expenditure by economic items for both development and recurrent expenditure.
heading_path: 1  INTRODUCTION

blocks.text: Chapter four presents analysis of MDAs' budget performance by sector for both development and recurrent expenditure. The sectors are; (i) Agriculture, Rural and Urban Development, (ii) Education, (iii) Energy, Infrastructure and Information Communications Technology, (iv) Environment Protection, Water and Natural Resources, (v) General Economic and Commercial Affairs (vi) Governance, Justice, Law and Order, (vii) Health, (viii) National Security, (ix) Public Administration and International Relations, and (x) Social Protection, Culture and Recreation. Information contained in this chapter includes revised gross and net estimates, exchequer issues, and expenditure per MDA and aggregate for each of the ten sectors. Chapter five provides a summary on programme performance by the MDAs and contains details on allocation of funds, expenditure for both development and recurrent programmes and implementation progress of each programme.
heading_path: 1  INTRODUCTION

blocks.text: The key challenges that affected budget implementation during the first nine months of the financial year are highlighted in Chapter six. Chapter seven provides the conclusion.

heading_path: 2.1.2 FY 2018/19 Revenue Estimates

blocks.text: The revised revenue estimates for FY 2018/19 amounted to Kshs.2.6 trillion, and was an increase compared to Kshs.2.3 trillion estimated in FY 2017/18. heading_path: 2.1.2 FY 2018/19 Revenue Estimates

blocks.text: 4.2 Agriculture, Rural and Urban Development (ARUD) Sector
heading_path: 4.2 Agriculture, Rural and Urban Development (ARUD) Sector

blocks.text: According to the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution of Kenya, Agriculture is a devolved function. The sector consists of seven MDAs namely: Ministry of Lands and Physical Planning (MoLPP); State Department for Crop Development; State Department for Irrigation; State Department for Agricultural Research; State Department for Livestock; State Department for Fisheries, Aquaculture and the Blue Economy and the National Land Commission (NLC), together with affiliated SAGAs and Training Institutions.
heading_path: 4.2 Agriculture, Rural and Urban Development (ARUD) Sector

blocks.text: The overall goal of the sector is to attain national food security and sustainable management of land and the Blue Economy. It is identified as one of the sectors that will drive delivery of the 10 per cent economic growth rate envisaged under the vision 2030 and accelerate attainment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The objectives of the sector are to: increase productivity and outputs in the sector, improve market access and trade; enhance national food security, sustainably exploit the Blue Economy, strengthen institutional capacity for improved service delivery, enhance the role of youth and women in the sector, enhance accessibility, equity and sustainable management of the land resource; and improve storage, access and retrieval of land and land resource data and information.
heading_path: 4.2 Agriculture, Rural and Urban Development (ARUD) Sector

blocks.text: The sector's revised budgetary allocation in FY 2018/19 is Kshs.52.5 billion and represents 2 per cent of the revised gross national budget, which is an increase from Kshs.48.5 billion allocated in FY 2017/18. The allocation comprised of Kshs.37 billion (70 per cent) for development budget and Kshs.15.5 billion (30 per cent) for recurrent expenditure. The State Department for Crop Development received the highest budgetary allocation of Kshs.23.4 billion (44.5 per cent of the sector's allocation), while National Land Commission had the lowest budgetary allocation of Kshs.1.2 billion (2.3 per cent).

blocks.text: The sector envisions a globally competitive education, training, research and innovation for sustainable development. heading_path: 4.4 Energy, Infrastructure and Information Communications Technology (EI & ICT) Sector

blocks.text: This sector consists of eight MDAs namely; State Department for: - Infrastructure, Transport, Shipping and Maritime, Housing and Urban Development, Public Works, Information Communication Technology, Broadcasting and Telecommunication, Petroleum and the Ministry of Energy.
heading_path: 4.4 Energy, Infrastructure and Information Communications Technology (EI & ICT) Sector

blocks.text: This sector is crucial for Kenya's economic transformation and sustained economic growth, development and poverty reduction. heading_path: 4.4 Energy, Infrastructure and Information Communications Technology (EI & ICT) Sector

blocks.text: The key strategic goals of the sector are to develop and maintain sustainable services to facilitate efficient movement of goods and people, develop and sustain access to opportunities in the shipping and maritime industry, improve universal access to information technology enabled services, improve access to competitive reliable and safe supply of petroleum products to all Kenyans, among others.

blocks.text: 4.5 Environment Protection, Water and Natural Resource Sector
heading_path: 4.5 Environment Protection, Water and Natural Resource Sector

blocks.text: The Environment Protection, Water and Natural Resources Sector consist of four MDAs namely: State Department for Environment and Forestry, Ministry of Water and Sanitation, State Department for Mining and State Department for Wildlife.
heading_path: 4.5 Environment Protection, Water and Natural Resource Sector

blocks.text: The overall goal of this sector is to ensure sustainable development in a clean and secure environment. Its specific objectives are to: enhance sustainable management of environment, water, irrigation and natural resources; ensure access to water and natural resources, benefit socio-economic development and enhance capacity building for environment, water and natural resources management. It also aims at increasing utilization of land through irrigation, drainage and land reclamation; enhance research on environment, water and natural resources for sustainable development, protect and reclaim the environment in order to establish a durable and sustainable system of development and resilience to climate change.

heading_path: 4.6 General Economic and Commercial Affairs (GECA) Sector

blocks.text: The General Economic and Commercial Affairs (GECA) sector consists of six MDAs, namely: State Department for Industrialization, Co-operatives, Trade, East African Community, Regional and Northern Corridor Development and Ministry of Tourism.
heading_path: 4.6 General Economic and Commercial Affairs (GECA) Sector

blocks.text: The Sector aims at creating employment opportunities and wealth creation for poverty reduction, fast tracking of the regional integration initiatives and promotion of equity among the Kenyan citizens. This is expected to be achieved through: creating an enabling environment for business, mobilization of resources for investments and industrial development, promotion of exports, promotion of sustainable tourism and deepening of the East Africa Community Integration.
heading_path: 4.6 General Economic and Commercial Affairs (GECA) Sector

blocks.text: The revised budgetary allocation to the Sector in FY 2018/19 is Kshs.34.6 billion, representing 1 per cent of the revised gross national budget. blocks.text: 4.7 Governance, Justice, Law and Order Sector (GJLOS)
heading_path: 4.7 Governance, Justice, Law and Order Sector (GJLOS)

blocks.text: The GJLOS sector consists of fifteen MDAs which include: State Department for Interior, State Department for Correctional Services, State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services, State Law Office and Department of Justice, The Judiciary, Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC), Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, Office of the Registrar of Political Parties, Witness Protection Agency (WPA), Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR), Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), Judicial Service Commission (JSC), National Police Service Commission (NPSC), National Gender and Equality Commission (NGEC), and the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).
heading_path: 4.7 Governance, Justice, Law and Order Sector (GJLOS)

blocks.text: The sector implements the following functions; provision of security, correctional services, legal advisory services to government agencies and administration of justice. It also plays a major role in promoting integrity and the fight against corruption, provision of prosecution services, regulating political parties, protecting witnesses and human rights. Further, the sector also plays an instrumental role in the delimitation of electoral boundaries and management of electoral process, promotion of gender equality, inclusion of marginalized groups and communities, and civilian policing oversight.
heading_path: 4.7 Governance, Justice, Law and Order Sector (GJLOS)

blocks.text: In addition, the sector plays a role in border management, peace building and conflict management, registration services, regulation of the gaming industry, provision of population management services, eradication of drugs and substance abuse, crime research and government printing services. It also plays a key role in ensuring achievement of national values, and promoting national cohesion.
heading_path: 4.7 Governance, Justice, Law and Order Sector (GJLOS)

blocks.text: The revised budgetary allocation to the sector in FY 2018/19 is Kshs.190.6 billion representing 6.4 per cent of revised gross national budget, a decrease compared to Kshs.216 billion allocated in FY 2017/18. The allocation comprised of Kshs.23.7 billion (12.5 per cent) for development expenditure and Kshs.166.8 billion (87.5 per cent) for recurrent expenditure. heading_path: 4.11  Social Protection, Culture and Recreation Sector

blocks.text: The Social Protection, Culture and Recreation Sector comprises of six State Departments namely: Sports, Culture and Heritage, Labour, Social Protection, Pensions and Senior Citizens Affairs, Development of Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASAL) and Gender Affairs.

blocks.text: The sector plays a major role in the country's transformation by promoting and exploiting Kenya's diverse culture and arts; enhancing Kenya's reading culture; regulation, development and promotion of
heading_path: 4.11  Social Protection, Culture and Recreation Sector

blocks.text: 6.1 Introduction
heading_path: 6.1 Introduction

blocks.text: This chapter highlights issues that affected budget implementation by MDAs in the first nine months of FY 2018/19. It further provides recommendations aimed at improving budget implementation in the future.
heading_path: 6.1 Introduction

blocks.text: 6.2 Key Issues and Recommendations
heading_path: 6.2 Key Issues and Recommendations

blocks.text: In the course of overseeing budget implementation, the Office identified the following key challenges.
heading_path: 6.2 Key Issues and Recommendations

blocks.text: 6.2.1 Delay in Submission of Budget Performance Reports to the Office of the Controller of Budget
heading_path: 6.2.1 Delay in Submission of Budget Performance Reports to the Office of the Controller of Budget

blocks.text: Article 228 (6) of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010 and Section 9 of the Controller of Budget Act, 2016 requires the Controller of Budget to submit to each House of Parliament a report on the implementation of budgets of the national and county governments every four months. The Controller of Budget's report is based on quarterly reports on financial and non-financial performance submitted by MDAs in line with Section 83 of the PFM Act, 2012.
heading_path: 6.2.1 Delay in Submission of Budget Performance Reports to the Office of the Controller of Budget

blocks.text: The Office experienced delays in submission of the quarterly reports by some MDAs. This affected timely reporting and consequently affected oversight of budget implementation by the various stakeholders.
heading_path: 6.2.1 Delay in Submission of Budget Performance Reports to the Office of the Controller of Budget

blocks.text: All MDAs should submit quarterly financial and non-financial performance reports to the OCOB within fifteen days following the end of each quarter in order to facilitate timely preparation and publication of budget implementation reports.
heading_path: 6.2.1 Delay in Submission of Budget Performance Reports to the Office of the Controller of Budget

blocks.text: 6.2.2 Failure to Align Budget Re-allocation to Actual Performance
heading_path: 6.2.2 Failure to Align Budget Re-allocation to Actual Performance

blocks.text: In the first nine months of FY 2018/19, Parliament approved Supplementary Budget I, which mainly rationalized budgetary allocations to non-core activities in order to release resources for implementation of development activities and the Big Four Agenda. While the budget revision was necessary, budget performance information such as exchequer issues and expenditure was not fully considered during the revision. As a result, some budget provisions were reduced below the level of expenditure already incurred.
heading_path: 6.2.2 Failure to Align Budget Re-allocation to Actual Performance

blocks.text: We recommend that, affected MDAs should liaise with the National Treasury to appropriately align budget allocations to performance through a supplementary budget for effective implementation.
heading_path: 6.2.2 Failure to Align Budget Re-allocation to Actual Performance

blocks.text: 7  CONCLUSION
heading_path: 7  CONCLUSION

blocks.text: This report has been prepared in fulfilment of Article 228(6) of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010 and Section 9 of the Controller of Budget Act, 2016. It provides information on the progress made in the implementation of the National Government budget in the first nine months of FY 2018/19.
heading_path: 7  CONCLUSION

blocks.text: Generally, the National Government registered improved budget performance compared to a similar period in the previous financial year. The Approved Supplementary Budget was Kshs.3 trillion in FY 2018/19 compared to Kshs.2.7 trillion in FY 2017/18, indicating growth in revenue and government expenditure. In the first nine months of the year, receipts into the Consolidated Fund amounted to Kshs.1.67 trillion, representing 64.8 per cent of the revised annual targets, an increase by 10.6 per cent compared to Kshs.1.51 trillion in the first nine months of FY 2017/18. Total exchequer issues to MDAs and County Governments amounted to Kshs.1.65 trillion, representing 64.4 per cent of the revised annual estimates, an increase of 20.4 per cent compared to Kshs.1.37 trillion in the first nine months of FY 2017/18.
heading_path: 7  CONCLUSION

blocks.text: Aggregate expenditure was Kshs.1.7 trillion, translating to an overall absorption rate of 63.5 per cent, an increase from 60.2 per cent (Kshs.1.3 trillion) recorded in a similar period in FY 2017/18. A total of Kshs.1.3 trillion was spent on recurrent expenditure, representing 67.7 per cent of the revised gross recurrent estimate and growth of 25.2 per cent compared to Kshs.1 trillion recorded in a similar period in FY 2017/18. Recurrent expenditure comprised of Kshs.720.6 billion incurred by MDAs and Kshs.584.2 billion towards Consolidated Fund Services. A total of Kshs.395.3 billion was spent on development expenditure representing an absorption rate of 60.8 per cent, indicating a growth of 39.8 per cent compared to Kshs.282.6 billion (46.7 per cent) recorded in the first nine months of FY 2017/18.
heading_path: 7  CONCLUSION

blocks.text: Despite the improved performance, the Office noted some challenges that affected budget implementation. These were; delay in submission of financial and non-financial reports to the Office of the Controller of Budget by Accounting Officers, which affected timely reporting and consequently  oversight by stakeholders; and failure to align budget re-allocation to actual performance during preparation of Supplementary Budget I, which led to reduction of some budget provisions below the level of expenditure already incurred. Therefore, affected MDAs should liaise with the National Treasury to appropriately align budget allocations to performance through a supplementary budget.
heading_path: 7  CONCLUSION

blocks.text: As mandated by the Constitution, the Office will continue to publish and publicize quarterly budget implementation review reports to inform Parliament, Executive, Stakeholders and members of the Public on the progress made in budget implementation .
heading_path: 7  CONCLUSION
